metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art keys — the dispatcher case at art:103-104 that execs runtime/scripts/check_keys.py with $@ forwarded. The Python script is 83 lines. It probes exactly one optional service (higgsfield CLI login) via `higgsfield account status` with a 25 s timeout, and writes one row into a table. Three status paths: valid (rc == 0), invalid (rc != 0, prints the failure text next to a fix line), unset (FileNotFoundError, prints 'CLI not installed'); a fourth `warn` path catches any other exception and flags the run inconclusive. Reads a repo-root .env via load_env (os.environ.setdefault, so the shell wins) but never prints a value — verified in demo/RUN-LOG.txt § 5 by grepping the output for a synthetic secret and getting zero matches. Two documentation drifts are called out honestly as the Teardown moment (B08): the docstring says 'Exit 1 if any present key is invalid' but line 40 declares any_invalid = False and never reassigns it, so exit is always 0; and the art help line at art:20 mentions 'SI key' but no SI probe exists in the script. Neither is a bug to fix in this reel — the point is that fellows should trust the live behavior, not the marketing copy. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation on 2026-09-09, machine higgsfield 0.2.3 installed, no active login, no .env in the toolkit tree. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 7c3b6abf2ec61bb70122fe12ba1e2d5bad049db19db16ddb3a1026cad274e8c6. beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher case. Two lines, no aliases, execs python3 check_keys.py with $@ forwarded.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case in the art file — two lines. Pattern 'keys', then exec python three on check_keys.py, with every argument forwarded. No aliases. Whatever the script decides is the whole command's behavior.

props.title: art:103-104 — one branch, no aliases
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # …
  keys)
    exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/check_keys.py" "$@"
    ;;
  # …
esac

# The wrapper: (1) resolves ART_HOME from art's own path,
# (2) execs the Python script, (3) forwards "$@" untouched.
# No aliases in the case block. The whole command surface
# is whatever check_keys.py decides to do.
props.sparkLine: One case. No aliases. One script.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK 2 — three status paths on the higgsfield probe, plus the fourth 'warn' fallback. The row(...) helper is the whole table primitive.
beats.narration_text: Four status paths, one probe. Return code zero — valid, green ready. Non-zero — invalid, red, with the exact fix line printed next to it. No such command on this box — unset, yellow, with a note that the free path runs silently. Any other exception — warn, and the whole run is flagged inconclusive. Each row is one line the human can read.

props.title: check_keys.py — four status paths, one probe
props.code:
# One helper appends one row per service:
def row(service, var, status, detail):
    rows.append((service, var, status, detail))

# The marks the table prints, from check_keys.py:66-67:
# valid            → "✅ valid"     (green)
# invalid          → "❌ invalid"   (red)
# unset            → "· unset"     (yellow)
# warn             → "⚠ check"     (yellow)
# set (not probed) → "· set"       (yellow)

# The higgsfield block is the only writer — the three-way
# branch decides which mark lands (see B06 for the body):
#   rc == 0                    → row(..., "valid",   out)
#   rc != 0                    → row(..., "invalid", "run `higgsfield auth login` — ...")
#   FileNotFoundError          → row(..., "unset",   "CLI not installed — ...")
#   any other Exception        → row(..., "warn",    f"status check failed: {e}")
props.sparkLine: One probe. Four marks. One row.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 1 — the whole higgsfield probe body, verbatim (check_keys.py:38-58). Three-way branch plus the fourth exception catch.
beats.narration_text: This is the whole probe. Twenty lines. A subprocess call with a twenty-five-second timeout. Return code zero writes the valid row. Non-zero writes the invalid row with the failure text quoted. A FileNotFoundError writes the unset row. Anything else — a broken pipe, a kernel signal, anything — flips the inconclusive flag and writes a warn row. That is every branch. There is no other service checked.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 2 — the .env loader and the redaction proof. load_env uses os.environ.setdefault (shell wins). Values are never printed — verified via a synthetic secret.
beats.narration_text: One more mechanism worth showing. The script reads a repo-root dot-env file, if one exists, via load_env — using os dot environ dot setdefault, so anything already in the shell wins. But it never prints a value. To prove it — write a fake secret into dot env, run the script, and grep the output for the secret. Zero matches. The dot env is scanned for keys the script wants; the values stay silent.

props.title: check_keys.py:20-30 + redaction proof
props.code:
def load_env():
    f = REPO / ".env"
    if not f.exists():
        return
    for line in f.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        k, v = line.split("=", 1)
        k = k.strip(); v = v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        os.environ.setdefault(k, v)   # shell wins

# Proof the values stay silent (demo/RUN-LOG.txt § 5, verbatim):
$ printf 'MY_SECRET=this-should-never-print\n' > .env
$ ART_HOME=$PWD python3 .../check_keys.py 2>&1 \
     | grep -c 'this-should-never-print'
0     # zero matches in the whole output. The .env is scanned,
      # the values never leave the process.
props.sparkLine: .env is read. Values never print. Proof: zero.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY / the design tell — docstring promises exit 1 on invalid, code declares any_invalid=False and never reassigns it. art:20 help mentions 'SI key' but no SI probe exists. Both are honestly named; neither is fixed in this reel.
beats.narration_text: One design tell worth calling out. The docstring says exit zero if every present key is valid, one if any is invalid. Read the code. The variable any underscore invalid is declared false on line forty and never reassigned. So the invalid branch does not actually flip the exit code. And the art help line advertises an 'SI key' check — grep the script for SI, and you get zero hits. So the surface promises two things the code does not enforce. Both are harmless today — nothing in the pipeline gates on this exit — but if you ever need to fail a CI job on a red row, you now know exactly which line to patch.

props.title: the design tell — two drifts
props.code:
# DRIFT 1 — the exit-code promise

# check_keys.py:8-10 (docstring):
#   "Exit 0 if every present key is valid; 1 if any present key
#    is invalid."

# check_keys.py:40 (main body):
    any_invalid = False
# …the variable is NEVER reassigned. The `invalid` branch just
# appends a red row and moves on. Exit is always 0 unless the
# probe itself throws.

# DRIFT 2 — the SI-key promise

# art:20 (dispatcher help block):
#   "./art keys   validate optional keys (Higgsfield login, SI key)"

$ grep -in 'si' runtime/scripts/check_keys.py | grep -v 'sys\|osi\|sit'
(no matches — the SI probe does not exist)

# Both drifts are harmless today. Nothing gates on this exit,
# and no build asks for an SI row. But if you ever want to fail
# CI on a red row, you now know: patch line 40 — set
# any_invalid = True inside the else branch.
props.sparkLine: Docstring promises. Code delivers one probe, exit 0.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art keys. A live probe of one optional CLI, wrapped in a two-line dispatcher case, that prints a colored table and always exits zero. The toolkit needs no keys. This command exists so a red row is visible before you go looking for it. Run it once when you clone the repo, and run it again the day you install Higgsfield. In between, ignore it.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt is INTERESTING (audit, do not fix). Narration reads it aloud and discusses why.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code, pointed at your own copy of the toolkit. Do not fix the script. Just audit it. Ask Claude to quote the docstring on lines eight to ten, name the exact variable that would need to change for the promise to hold, and write one pytest test that would fail on the current code and pass if the promise were kept. Then ask whether the 'SI key' phrase in the art help still refers to anything that exists. Look for whether Claude is tempted to just patch the file. Reading is not fixing. Notice first, then decide.

(4) Write ONE pytest-style test that would FAIL against the current code and PASS if the promise were kept — no fix, just the test. (5) Tell me whether the ./art help line about 'SI key' refers to anything currently probed by the script.
